components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这只狗对主人非常忠诚。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu duì zhǔrén fēicháng zhōngchéng.
example.english: This dog is extremely loyal to its owner.
example.fact: 主 by itself already carries the sense "main, principal" (主要, "main"), tracing back to a pictograph of the flame atop an oil lamp — the part everyone's eyes are drawn to — and 主人 extends that "central, principal figure" image from an object to a person: the owner, host, or master of a place.

examples.hanzi: 这家饭店的主人很热情。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn de zhǔrén hěn rèqíng.
examples.english: The owner of this restaurant is very warm.

examples.hanzi: 主人请大家坐下来喝茶。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔrén qǐng dàjiā zuò xiàlái hē chá.
examples.english: The host invited everyone to sit down for tea.

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.

example.pinyin: Qǐng tián yíxià zhè zhāng biǎo.
example.english: Please fill in this form.
example.fact: In simplified writing 表 merges several old characters: surface (表面), form (表格), a watch (手表) and "to show" (表示). 表哥 and 表妹 are cousins through the mother or sisters, not the father's side.

examples.hanzi: 请在表格上写好你的名字。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài biǎogé shang xiěhǎo nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please write your name on the form.

examples.hanzi: 这块手表是我爸爸送的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài shǒubiǎo shì wǒ bàba sòng de.
examples.english: My dad gave me this wristwatch.

components.note: 釆 (distinguish) — sorting things out: 释 is to untangle and explain.
圣 stands in for 睪 in the traditional 釋; the same part is in 译 yì, 泽 zé and 择 zé.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 经过调查,警方释放了那名嫌疑人。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò diàochá, jǐngfāng shìfàng le nà míng xiányírén.
example.english: After the investigation, the police released the suspect.
example.fact: Beyond freeing a person, 释放 extends naturally into physics and chemistry for "to release" energy or a substance (释放能量, "to release energy") and into everyday psychology for releasing emotion (释放压力, "to relieve stress") — one verb spanning legal, scientific, and emotional registers that English usually splits across "release," "discharge," and "vent."

examples.hanzi: 医生让他把压力释放出来。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng ràng tā bǎ yālì shìfàng chūlái.
examples.english: The doctor told him to release his stress.

examples.hanzi: 工厂释放出很多有害气体。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng shìfàng chū hěn duō yǒuhài qìtǐ.
examples.english: The factory released a lot of harmful gas.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
行 (go, road) — 行 (walk, go) splits around the middle — 街 is a road; compare 往 go and 衔.
圭 (guī) — loose hint only — 街 is jiē.

example.hanzi: 周末的时候,大街上人特别多。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò de shíhou, dàjiē shàng rén tèbié duō.
example.english: On weekends, the main street is especially crowded.
example.fact: 大街 names a wide, major thoroughfare, as opposed to a narrow 小巷 or 胡同 ("alley, lane") — and the fixed phrase 大街小巷 ("big streets, small lanes") is Mandarin's idiomatic way of saying "everywhere in town," pairing the two extremes of street width to mean total coverage.

examples.hanzi: 我们在大街上遇到了一位老朋友。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài dàjiē shang yùdào le yí wèi lǎo péngyou.
examples.english: We met an old friend on the street.

examples.hanzi: 这条大街两边都是商店。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dàjiē liǎng biān dōu shì shāngdiàn.
examples.english: There are shops on both sides of this street.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree 木 boxed in by an enclosure 囗: trapped, hemmed in; hence 困难 difficulty.

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn kùn, xiǎng shuìjiào.
example.english: I am sleepy and want to sleep.
example.fact: In daily speech 困 mostly means "sleepy", whereas 累 means "tired"; 我很困 is about wanting to sleep. In writing it means trapped or in hardship: 被困 (trapped) and 困难 (difficulty).

examples.hanzi: 他一天没睡觉，现在很困。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì tiān méi shuìjiào, xiànzài hěn kùn.
examples.english: He hasn't slept all day and is very sleepy now.

examples.hanzi: 他们被大雪困在山上了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen bèi dàxuě kùn zài shān shang le.
examples.english: They were trapped on the mountain by the heavy snow.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 竹 (bamboo) as in 笔, 筷, 篮; boxes and baskets were woven from bamboo, so 箱 is a box or chest.
相 (xiāng) — same sound — 箱 is xiāng, just like 相.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 她把所有衣服都装进了箱子里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ suǒyǒu yīfu dōu zhuāngjìn le xiāngzi lǐ.
example.english: She packed all her clothes into the suitcase.
example.fact: 箱's bamboo radical ⺮ reveals that the character originally named a woven bamboo chest, long before cardboard or hard-shell suitcases existed — the same radical shows up across a whole family of container words, like 篮子 ("basket"), that trace back to bamboo construction.

examples.hanzi: 这个箱子太重了,我搬不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāngzi tài zhòng le, wǒ bān bú dòng.
examples.english: This box is too heavy, I can't move it.

examples.hanzi: 请把箱子放在门口。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xiāngzi fàng zài ménkǒu.
examples.english: Please put the box by the door.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — the left part and radical, as in 听 listen. 耶 mostly writes foreign names (耶稣 Jesus), so the ear is only a shape hint.
阝 (city) — the right part, as in 都 and 那. It does not give the sound here. Memory aid: an ear in a foreign city hearing a new name.
鱼 (fish) — the left part and radical, as in 鲜 fresh. In 稣 it is just a visible part; the character is mostly seen in 耶稣 Jesus. Memory aid: a fish.
禾 (grain) — the right part, as in 和 and 秋. The dictionary lists grain as the hint; the 'revive' meaning is not explained by the shape.

example.hanzi: 很多人在圣诞节庆祝耶稣的诞生。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén zài Shèngdànjié qìngzhù Yēsū de dànshēng.
example.english: Many people celebrate the birth of Jesus at Christmas.
example.fact: 耶稣 is a pure phonetic transliteration — 耶 and 稣 were chosen purely for their sound (yē and sū) to approximate "Jesus," with no regard for their literal meanings — the same non-meaning-based borrowing strategy used for other foreign names and loanwords like 咖啡 (kāfēi, "coffee").

examples.hanzi: 耶稣是基督教的中心人物。
examples.pinyin: Yēsū shì Jīdūjiào de zhōngxīn rénwù.
examples.english: Jesus is the central figure of Christianity.

examples.hanzi: 这幅画画的是耶稣和他的朋友们。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà huà de shì Yēsū hé tā de péngyoumen.
examples.english: This painting depicts Jesus and his friends.

components.note: 由 (from, reason) — mostly useful as a sound part: 油 yóu, 邮 yóu, 柚 yòu, 抽 chōu all contain it.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 由于天气不好,比赛被取消了。
example.pinyin: Yóuyú tiānqì bù hǎo, bǐsài bèi qǔxiāo le.
example.english: Due to bad weather, the match was cancelled.
example.fact: 由于 sits at the more formal, written end of Mandarin's "because" spectrum — the kind of connector expected in a news report or official statement — while 因为 is the neutral, everyday default used just as easily in casual conversation.

examples.hanzi: 由于堵车,我迟到了十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyú dǔchē, wǒ chídào le shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: Because of the traffic, I was ten minutes late.

examples.hanzi: 这件事由于他的帮助才成功了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yóuyú tā de bāngzhù cái chénggōng le.
examples.english: This succeeded thanks to his help.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家 home, 室 room, 安 safe; 宣 was a large hall, where proclamations are made.
巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.

example.hanzi: 校长在大会上宣布了新的规定。
example.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zài dàhuì shàng xuānbù le xīn de guīdìng.
example.english: The principal announced the new regulations at the assembly.
example.fact: 宣 alone already carries the sense of a grand, public proclamation — its old form pictures a wide hall radiating outward, evoking a palace where royal edicts were announced — so 宣布, adding 布 ("to spread out, to distribute"), literally means "to proclaim and spread wide," fitting for announcements meant to reach a broad audience.

examples.hanzi: 老师宣布明天不用上课。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī xuānbù míngtiān bú yòng shàngkè.
examples.english: The teacher announced there would be no class tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 公司宣布了新的休假计划。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xuānbù le xīn de xiūjià jìhuà.
examples.english: The company announced a new vacation plan.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 执 is to hold or grasp, then carry out, as in 执行.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 这个计划已经开始执行了。
example.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà yǐjīng kāishǐ zhíxíng le.
example.english: This plan has already started to be implemented.
example.fact: 执 alone means "to hold firmly, to grasp" (as in 执照, "license," literally something one holds as proof) — 执行 extends that grip onto action itself, "to hold firmly to and carry through" a plan, order, or law, distinct from 实行 which leans more toward putting a general policy into practice.

examples.hanzi: 你要认真执行老板的决定。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào rènzhēn zhíxíng lǎobǎn de juédìng.
examples.english: You must carry out the boss's decision carefully.

examples.hanzi: 这条规定从下个月开始执行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo guīdìng cóng xià ge yuè kāishǐ zhíxíng.
examples.english: This rule takes effect next month.

meanings: to report sth to the police

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.

example.hanzi: 发现有人闯入后,她立刻报警了。
example.pinyin: Fāxiàn yǒu rén chuǎngrù hòu, tā lìkè bàojǐng le.
example.english: After discovering someone had broken in, she immediately called the police.
example.fact: 警 is the root behind Mandarin's whole police/alarm vocabulary — 警察 ("police"), 警车 ("police car"), 报警 ("to report to police, to sound an alarm") — all built on a character whose phonetic component 敬 originally lent it a sense of urgent respect or caution.

examples.hanzi: 邻居家被偷了,他们马上报警了。
examples.pinyin: Línjū jiā bèi tōu le, tāmen mǎshàng bàojǐng le.
examples.english: The neighbor's home was broken into and they called the police right away.

examples.hanzi: 如果你遇到危险,可以拨打电话报警。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ yùdào wēixiǎn, kěyǐ bōdǎ diànhuà bàojǐng.
examples.english: If you are in danger, you can call the police.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí jiàn hěn guì de lǐwù.
example.english: This is a very expensive gift.
example.fact: 物 is a bound form meaning thing: 礼物 (gift), 动物, 植物, 食物, 物价 (prices), 物理 (physics). For "thing" in speech Chinese uses 东西; 物 is the written-register counterpart.

examples.hanzi: 我想送她一件生日礼物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng sòng tā yí jiàn shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: I want to give her a birthday gift.

examples.hanzi: 这里的物价不太高。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de wùjià bú tài gāo.
examples.english: Prices here aren't very high.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.

example.hanzi: 你这样算数不对,再检查一下。
example.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng suànshù bú duì, zài jiǎnchá yíxià.
example.english: You calculated this wrong, check it again.
example.fact: 不对 is also a common stand-alone exclamation for catching a mistake mid-sentence — much like English "wait, no" — as when a speaker corrects themselves ("不对,不对,是三点,不是两点", "No wait, it's three o'clock, not two") rather than only describing a statement as objectively false.

examples.hanzi: 这个答案不对,你再想一想。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dá'àn búduì, nǐ zài xiǎng yi xiǎng.
examples.english: This answer is wrong, think about it again.

examples.hanzi: 我觉得他说的有点儿不对。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde tā shuō de yǒudiǎnr búduì.
examples.english: I think what he said is a little off.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.
石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破, 研, 砖; 码 first meant stone weights, then numbers.
马 (mǎ) sounds exactly like 码; also in 吗, 骂 mà, 妈 mā.

example.pinyin: Qǐng shūrù nǐ de zhànghù mìmǎ.
example.english: Please enter your account password.
example.fact: 码 is Mandarin's general word for "a numerical code" — it also shows up in 号码 ("number," as in a phone number) and 条码 ("barcode") — while 密 contributes "secret, dense, close" (as in 秘密, "secret"), so 密码 literally combines "secret" with "code" into today's word for password or cipher.

examples.hanzi: 我忘了手机的密码。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàng le shǒujī de mìmǎ.
examples.english: I forgot my phone's password.

examples.hanzi: 这个密码太简单了,容易被别人猜到。
examples.pinyin: Zhège mìmǎ tài jiǎndān le, róngyì bèi biérén cāi dào.
examples.english: This password is too simple and easy for others to guess.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 (silk); colours came from dyed silk, as in 绿, 紫, 给.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 红 is hóng; 工 also sounds out 江 jiāng and 空 kōng.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一条红色的裙子。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yì tiáo hóngsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She's wearing a red skirt.
example.fact: Beyond the plain color, 红色 carries a heavy political charge in Mandarin — shorthand for the Chinese Communist Party and revolutionary history, as in 红色旅游 ("red tourism," visiting revolutionary historical sites) and 又红又专 ("both red and expert," a Mao-era ideal pairing political loyalty with technical skill) — a symbolic weight most color words in English don't carry.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢红色的苹果。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan hóngsè de píngguǒ.
examples.english: I like red apples.

examples.hanzi: 春节的时候,家里到处都是红色的灯笼。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié de shíhou, jiā lǐ dàochù dōu shì hóngsè de dēnglong.
examples.english: During Spring Festival, there are red lanterns everywhere at home.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑 ride, 驾; 骗 first meant to jump on a horse.
扁 (biǎn) — near sound — 骗 is piàn; 扁 also sounds out 偏 piān, 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那个人是个骗子,别相信他。
example.pinyin: Nàge rén shì gè piànzi, bié xiāngxìn tā.
example.english: That person is a swindler, don't believe him.
example.fact: 骗 alone means "to deceive, to swindle," and its horse radical 马 traces back to an old image of swinging up onto a horse — perhaps an unexpectedly quick trick — which later drifted into the entirely figurative sense of tricking someone out of money or trust that 骗子 carries today.

examples.hanzi: 别听他的,他就是个骗子。
examples.pinyin: Bié tīng tā de, tā jiù shì ge piànzi.
examples.english: Don't listen to him, he's just a swindler.

examples.hanzi: 那个骗子骗了很多老人的钱。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge piànzi piàn le hěn duō lǎorén de qián.
examples.english: That con man cheated many old people out of their money.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 财, 费; 货 is goods that are traded.
化 (huà) — near sound — 货 is huò; 化 also sounds out 花 huā.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de huò hěn xīn.
example.english: This shop's stock is very new.
example.fact: 货 means goods to be bought or sold: 送货 (to deliver), 进货 (to restock), 货币 (currency). As slang it is an insult, as in 蠢货 (idiot) or 你这个货.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的货物很全。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de huòwù hěn quán.
examples.english: This store has a full range of goods.

examples.hanzi: 货车把东西运到了仓库。
examples.pinyin: Huòchē bǎ dōngxi yùn dào le cāngkù.
examples.english: The truck delivered the goods to the warehouse.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān de kōngjiān bú dà.
example.english: This room doesn't have much space.
example.fact: 间 is pictured as 门 (a door/gate) with 日 (the sun) — literally sunlight slipping through a doorway — which supplies the "gap, in-between" image that 空间 pairs with 空 ("empty") to build "space"; the same 间 carries that gap sense into 中间 ("in the middle") and 时间 ("time").

examples.hanzi: 我们的客厅空间很大,可以放一架钢琴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de kètīng kōngjiān hěn dà, kěyǐ fàng yí jià gāngqín.
examples.english: Our living room has plenty of space for a piano.

examples.hanzi: 这份工作给了我很大的发展空间。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò gěi le wǒ hěn dà de fāzhǎn kōngjiān.
examples.english: This job gives me a lot of room to grow.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 折 shows a hand swinging an axe 斤, so to chop or snap, then to fold and bend.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 析 and 新; it is the cutting tool.
石 (stone) — 石 is stone, as in 破 break, 砖 brick; 磨 is a millstone and the act of grinding.
麻 (má) — near sound — 磨 is mó; 麻 also sounds out 摩 mó and 魔 mó.

example.pinyin: Bìngtòng zhémó le tā hǎojǐ nián.
example.english: The illness tormented him for several years.
example.fact: 折 (from 扌 "hand" plus 斤 "axe" — literally "to snap in two by hand") and 磨 (from 石 "stone," "to grind with a millstone") combine into a vivid image of being broken and ground down, which fits both the physical and the psychological senses 折磨 carries today.

examples.hanzi: 失眠折磨得她每天都很累。
examples.pinyin: Shīmián zhémó de tā měi tiān dōu hěn lèi.
examples.english: Insomnia leaves her exhausted every day.

examples.hanzi: 别折磨自己了,这不是你的错。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhémó zìjǐ le, zhè bú shì nǐ de cuò.
examples.english: Stop torturing yourself, it's not your fault.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — marks liquids and things that flow, as in 河 river, 汤 soup, 酒 liquor; here an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) sounds exactly like 油 — the same sound clue appears in 邮 yóu and 柚 yòu.

example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào fàng tài duō yóu.
example.english: Please don't put in too much oil.
example.fact: 油 covers cooking oil (食用油), petrol (汽油) and crude oil (石油). 加油 literally means to add oil, so it is both what you do at a petrol station and the cheer "go for it!".

examples.hanzi: 他的车没有油了，我们得去加油站。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chē méiyǒu yóu le, wǒmen děi qù jiāyóuzhàn.
examples.english: His car is out of gas, so we need to go to a gas station.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜太油了，我吃不下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài tài yóu le, wǒ chībuxià.
examples.english: This dish is too greasy for me to eat.

components.note: 尸 (body) — originally a person seated or lying; as a radical it is in 尾 tail, 层 floor, 居 reside, 屋 house.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá fāxiàn le yí jù shītǐ.
example.english: The police found a body.
example.fact: 尸 is nearly always used in 尸体 (corpse); the measure word for corpses is 具. The same shape is also a common radical on top of characters like 屋 (house) and 层 (storey), where it has little to do with corpses.

examples.hanzi: 尸体已经被送到了医院。
examples.pinyin: Shītǐ yǐjīng bèi sòng dào le yīyuàn.
examples.english: The body has already been taken to the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 他是在尸检以后才知道原因的。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zài shījiǎn yǐhòu cái zhīdào yuányīn de.
examples.english: He learned the cause only after the autopsy.

components.note: 留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.pinyin: Tā bú zài, wǒ gěi tā liúyán le.
example.english: He's not in, so I left him a message.
example.fact: 留言 is transparently "words (言) left behind (留)" — a pre-digital word that absorbed new technology wholesale rather than being replaced, so it now covers a scribbled note, a 语音留言 (voicemail), and a comment left on a website alike.

examples.hanzi: 你有事的话,可以给我留言。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shì de huà, kěyǐ gěi wǒ liúyán.
examples.english: If you need anything, you can leave me a message.

examples.hanzi: 我看到了你昨天晚上的留言。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kàndào le nǐ zuótiān wǎnshang de liúyán.
examples.english: I saw your message from last night.

components.note: 能 (néng) — 能 was originally a picture of a bear, which is why it sits in 熊; the 灬 below is fire dots, 熊 is the bear, as in 熊猫 panda.

example.pinyin: Xióng xǐhuan chī fēngmì.
example.english: Bears like to eat honey.
example.fact: 熊猫 (panda) literally means "bear cat". The measure word is 只 or 头. In spoken Chinese 熊 is also slang for wimpy or useless: 你真熊 means "you are such a wimp".

examples.hanzi: 动物园里有一只大熊。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī dà xióng.
examples.english: There is a big bear in the zoo.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢的动物是熊猫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de dòngwù shì xióngmāo.
examples.english: My favorite animal is the panda.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn jiālǐ de wèidao.
example.english: I really miss the taste of home.
example.fact: 念 is built from 今 ("now, the present") over 心 ("heart/mind") — literally "what's presently on the heart." Paired with 想 ("to think of"), 想念 leans more wistful and literary than bare 想 alone, which can express a lighter, more casual "miss" (想你 vs. the more heartfelt 想念你).

examples.hanzi: 出国以后,我很想念我的朋友们。
examples.pinyin: Chūguó yǐhòu, wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn wǒ de péngyoumen.
examples.english: Since going abroad, I've missed my friends a lot.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们都很想念奶奶做的饺子。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen dōu hěn xiǎngniàn nǎinai zuò de jiǎozi.
examples.english: The kids all miss the dumplings Grandma makes.

components.note: 而 (and, but) — oldest form is a beard (compare 须 xū, beard), later borrowed for the conjunction; 而 survives in 耐 nài.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 对我而言,健康比金钱更重要。
example.pinyin: Duì wǒ éryán, jiànkāng bǐ jīnqián gèng zhòngyào.
example.english: As far as I'm concerned, health matters more than money.
example.fact: 而言 almost never stands alone — it lives inside the fixed frame "对 X 而言" ("as far as X is concerned"), a more formal, written-register alternative to the everyday "对 X 来说"; learners rarely need it outside that one frame.

examples.hanzi: 就价格而言,这家店最便宜。
examples.pinyin: Jiù jiàgé ér yán, zhè jiā diàn zuì piányi.
examples.english: In terms of price, this store is the cheapest.

examples.hanzi: 总的而言,这次旅行很愉快。
examples.pinyin: Zǒng de ér yán, zhè cì lǚxíng hěn yúkuài.
examples.english: Overall, this trip was very pleasant.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 值 is worth.
直 (zhí) sounds exactly like 值; also 植 zhí and 置 zhì.

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū zhí wǔshí kuài qián.
example.english: This book is worth fifty yuan.
example.fact: 值 is "to be worth": 值钱 (valuable), 值得 (worth doing), 价值 (value). 值班 means to be on duty or on shift, because 值 also means "to take one's turn".

examples.hanzi: 这个办法值得一试。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ zhídé yí shì.
examples.english: This method is worth a try.

examples.hanzi: 今晚谁值班？
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn shéi zhíbān?
examples.english: Who is on duty tonight?

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 信; 倍 is doubling, as in 加倍 and 两倍.
咅 (pǒu) — only a loose sound hint (bèi vs pǒu); same part sits in 部 bù and 培 péi.

example.pinyin: Tā de gōngzī shì wǒ de liǎng bèi.
example.english: His salary is twice mine.
example.fact: 倍 is a multiplier: 两倍 (twice), 三倍 (three times). With a verb like 增加, 增加了一倍 means "doubled", but 增加了两倍 is ambiguous (tripled or doubled?), so careful writers say 增加到.

examples.hanzi: 今年的价格是去年的三倍。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de jiàgé shì qùnián de sān bèi.
examples.english: This year's price is three times last year's.

examples.hanzi: 他加倍努力，终于考上了大学。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiābèi nǔlì, zhōngyú kǎo shàng le dàxué.
examples.english: He worked twice as hard and finally got into university.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 擦 is rubbing and wiping.
察 (chá) — loose sound hint (cā vs chá); same part in 察 chá and 嚓 cā.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi cā gānjìng.
example.english: Please wipe the table clean.
example.fact: 擦 covers wiping (擦桌子), rubbing on (擦药, apply ointment) and brushing past (擦伤, graze; 擦肩而过, to pass by each other closely). 橡皮擦 is an eraser.

examples.hanzi: 他在擦黑板。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài cā hēibǎn.
examples.english: He is wiping the blackboard.

examples.hanzi: 别忘了擦干净你的手。
examples.pinyin: Bié wàng le cā gānjìng nǐ de shǒu.
examples.english: Don't forget to wipe your hands clean.

components.note: 尢 (bent leg) — the dictionary radical, a stroke group once meaning a lame person. It does not explain 尤其 'especially' today.
丶 (dot) — the extra stroke on 尢. Memory aid: one dot added to 尢 makes it stand out, hence 'especially'.
其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢水果,尤其是芒果。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan shuǐguǒ, yóuqí shì mángguǒ.
example.english: I like fruit, especially mangoes.
example.fact: 尤其 is almost always followed by 是 (尤其是, "especially [is]") when it singles out one example from a larger category — dropping the 是 is grammatical but noticeably less common in natural speech.

examples.hanzi: 夏天很热,尤其是在中午。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān hěn rè, yóuqí shì zài zhōngwǔ.
examples.english: Summer is hot, especially at noon.

examples.hanzi: 这件事尤其重要,请别忘了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yóuqí zhòngyào, qǐng bié wàng le.
examples.english: This matter is especially important, so please don't forget.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a figure curled up gives the idea of rolling; 卷 sounds out 圈 quān, 拳 quán and 倦 juàn.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ dìtú juǎn qǐlai le.
example.english: He rolled up the map.
example.fact: 卷 is juǎn when it means to roll (卷发, curly hair) and juàn when it means a scroll, volume or exam paper (试卷). The 2020s buzzword 内卷 ("involution") means rat-race competition, also read juǎn.

examples.hanzi: 他把纸卷成了一个筒。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhǐ juǎnchéngle yí gè tǒng.
examples.english: He rolled the paper into a tube.

examples.hanzi: 风把灰尘卷了起来。
examples.pinyin: Fēng bǎ huīchén juǎn le qǐlái.
examples.english: The wind swirled the dust up.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 他在这个行业有十年的经验。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhège hángyè yǒu shí nián de jīngyàn.
example.english: He has ten years of experience in this industry.
example.fact: 经验 names practical experience built up by doing something over time (十年经验, "ten years' experience"), while its near-cousin 体验 is the more subjective, momentary experience of undergoing something, like a ride or an emotion — a distinction English's single word "experience" collapses.

examples.hanzi: 我没有带孩子的经验。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu dài háizi de jīngyàn.
examples.english: I have no experience taking care of children.

examples.hanzi: 这次失败也是一次宝贵的经验。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shībài yě shì yí cì bǎoguì de jīngyàn.
examples.english: This failure is also a valuable lesson.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 皿 is a dish or container, as in 盘 plate, 盖 cover, 益; 盒 is a box.
合 (hé) — same sound — 盒 is hé, matching 合; 合 also sounds out 哈 hā.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 她把照片放进一个盒子里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhàopiàn fàng jìn yí gè hézi lǐ.
example.english: She put the photos into a box.
example.fact: 盒 is built from 皿 ("dish, container") under the phonetic 合 (hé, which itself means "to close, to fit together") — a box is, after all, a container that closes, so the phonetic half happens to carry a scrap of meaning too.

examples.hanzi: 这个盒子里装着什么?
examples.pinyin: Zhège hézi lǐ zhuāng zhe shénme?
examples.english: What is in this box?

examples.hanzi: 他给女朋友买了一盒巧克力,放在漂亮的盒子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi nǚ péngyou mǎi le yì hé qiǎokèlì, fàng zài piàoliang de hézi lǐ.
examples.english: He bought his girlfriend chocolates in a pretty box.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood — cups were first made of wood, as in 桌, 板, 树.
不 (bù) — loose hint — 杯 is bēi; 不 shares just the b- start.

example.hanzi: 大家举起杯子,喊道:“干杯!”
example.pinyin: Dàjiā jǔqǐ bēizi, hǎndào: “Gānbēi!”
example.english: Everyone raised their glasses and shouted, "Cheers!"
example.fact: 干杯 literally means "dry cup" (干 "dry" + 杯 "cup") — the toast's implicit instruction is to empty the glass entirely, the same logic behind the English "bottoms up," so the literal and idiomatic senses line up almost exactly.

examples.hanzi: 来,为我们的友谊干杯!
examples.pinyin: Lái, wèi wǒmen de yǒuyì gānbēi!
examples.english: Come on, let's drink to our friendship!

examples.hanzi: 他喝了一点儿酒,但没有干杯。
examples.pinyin: Tā hē le yìdiǎnr jiǔ, dàn méiyǒu gānbēi.
examples.english: He had a little wine but didn't drink a toast.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — marks boats and ships, as in 船 ship, 航 sail; 艘 is the measure word for ships.
叟 (sǒu) — close sound: 艘 sōu. 叟 also sounds out 搜 sōu and 嫂 sǎo.

example.pinyin: Gǎngkǒu lǐ tíng zhe sān sōu dà chuán.
example.english: Three large ships are docked in the harbour.
example.fact: 艘 is the measure word for ships and larger vessels: 一艘轮船, 一艘航空母舰. Small boats are usually counted with 条 or 只 instead.

examples.hanzi: 那艘船开往海的另一边。
examples.pinyin: Nà sōu chuán kāiwǎng hǎi de lìng yì biān.
examples.english: That ship is heading to the other side of the sea.

examples.hanzi: 海上有一艘大轮船。
examples.pinyin: Hǎi shang yǒu yì sōu dà lúnchuán.
examples.english: There is a large steamship at sea.

meanings: way of looking at a thing

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 每个人对这件事都有不同的看法。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén duì zhè jiàn shì dōu yǒu bùtóng de kànfǎ.
example.english: Everyone has a different view on this matter.
example.fact: 看法 literally means "a way (法) of looking (看)" — one of several Chinese abstract nouns for "opinion" built directly on a verb of perception, the same pattern behind 想法 ("way of thinking," idea) and 说法 ("way of saying," account/version).

examples.hanzi: 你对这个问题有什么看法?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ duì zhège wèntí yǒu shénme kànfǎ?
examples.english: What's your take on this issue?

examples.hanzi: 我的看法跟你不一样。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de kànfǎ gēn nǐ bù yíyàng.
examples.english: My view is different from yours.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 肚 belly, 脚 foot, 脸 face, 胖 fat; 脑 is the brain.
The right half shows hair over a skull and also sounds out 恼 nǎo and 瑙 nǎo.

example.hanzi: 睡眠对大脑健康很重要。
example.pinyin: Shuìmián duì dànǎo jiànkāng hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: Sleep is very important for brain health.
example.fact: 大脑 technically names the cerebrum specifically, as distinct from 小脑 (the cerebellum) and 脑干 (the brainstem) — but in everyday speech it is used loosely for "the brain" as a whole, the way English "brain" glosses over the same anatomical distinction.

examples.hanzi: 学习新东西对大脑很有好处。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí xīn dōngxi duì dànǎo hěn yǒu hǎochù.
examples.english: Learning new things is good for the brain.

examples.hanzi: 他的大脑反应得很快。
examples.pinyin: Tā de dànǎo fǎnyìng de hěn kuài.
examples.english: His brain reacts very quickly.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen gòng yǒu èrshí ge xuésheng.
example.english: We have twenty students in all.
example.fact: 共 as an adverb means "altogether": 一共, 共计. It forms 共同 (common, joint), 共享 (to share) and 共和国 (republic). The party name 共产党 means "common-property party".

examples.hanzi: 我们共同努力，一定能成功。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gòngtóng nǔlì, yídìng néng chénggōng.
examples.english: If we work together, we can surely succeed.

examples.hanzi: 这个学期我们共学了五课。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xuéqī wǒmen gòng xué le wǔ kè.
examples.english: We studied five lessons in total this semester.

components.note: 罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhuāzhù le nàge zuìfàn.
example.english: The police caught the criminal.
example.fact: 罪 (from 罒 "net" over 非 "wrong") pictures wrongdoing caught in a net, and 犯 (from 犭, evoking an attacking animal) names the act of violating a rule — 罪犯 stacks "the crime" and "the violator" together into a single word for the person, not the act.

examples.hanzi: 罪犯已经被带走了。
examples.pinyin: Zuìfàn yǐjīng bèi dàizǒu le.
examples.english: The criminal has already been taken away.

examples.hanzi: 这个罪犯被判了五年。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zuìfàn bèi pàn le wǔ nián.
examples.english: This criminal was sentenced to five years.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 从这里到车站不到十分钟。
example.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào chēzhàn búdào shí fēnzhōng.
example.english: It's less than ten minutes from here to the station.
example.fact: 不到 attaches to a number or quantity to mean "less than, not quite reaching" (不到十分钟, "less than ten minutes") — literally 不 ("not") plus the verb 到 ("to arrive/reach"), a compact way to state an upper bound without a separate word like English "less than."

examples.hanzi: 我家离学校不到一公里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào bú dào yì gōnglǐ.
examples.english: My home is less than a kilometer from the school.

examples.hanzi: 她才来不到一个星期,就已经习惯了。
examples.pinyin: Tā cái lái bú dào yí ge xīngqī, jiù yǐjīng xíguàn le.
examples.english: She's been here less than a week and has already gotten used to it.

components.note: 门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ qù wènwen lǎoshī.
example.english: You can go ask the teacher about it.
example.fact: 问问 is simply 问 ("to ask") reduplicated, a common Mandarin device that softens a one-syllable verb into something brief or casual — the same pattern behind 看看 ("take a quick look") and 想想 ("think it over"). It is more a live grammatical process than a fixed dictionary word, which is why standard dictionaries often skip giving it its own entry.

examples.hanzi: 不懂的话,可以问问同学。
examples.pinyin: Bù dǒng de huà, kěyǐ wènwen tóngxué.
examples.english: If you don't understand, you can ask your classmates.

examples.hanzi: 我去问问价格,马上回来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù wènwen jiàgé, mǎshàng huílái.
examples.english: I'll go ask about the price and be right back.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 我们得想办法干掉这个对手。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen děi xiǎng bànfǎ gàndiào zhège duìshǒu.
example.english: We need to find a way to get rid of this rival.
example.fact: 干掉 pairs the colloquial, all-purpose 干 ("to do," the same 干 in slangy 干什么, "what are you doing") with 掉 used as an "away/off" verb complement, the same role it plays in 扔掉 ("throw away") and 卖掉 ("sell off") — together they read almost like the English slang "do away with."

examples.hanzi: 他想把这些垃圾邮件全都干掉。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ zhèxiē lājī yóujiàn quán dōu gàndiào.
examples.english: He wants to get rid of all this spam mail.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏里,你得先干掉最后的敌人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì lǐ, nǐ děi xiān gàndiào zuìhòu de dírén.
examples.english: In this game, you first have to take out the final enemy.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding the reins.
空 (kōng) is a close sound clue for kòng; 空 also in 腔 qiāng and 孔 kǒng.

example.pinyin: Tā bèi zhǐkòng tōuqiè.
example.english: He was accused of theft.
example.fact: 指控 sits at the formal, legal end of Chinese's "accuse" vocabulary — closer to a courtroom "to charge, to indict" than the everyday 怪 ("to blame") — so it shows up heavily in news and legal reporting rather than casual conversation.

examples.hanzi: 警方指控他参与了这起案件。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhǐkòng tā cānyù le zhè qǐ ànjiàn.
examples.english: The police accused him of being involved in this case.

examples.hanzi: 这些指控都没有证据。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē zhǐkòng dōu méiyǒu zhèngjù.
examples.english: None of these charges has any evidence.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 地球是一个美丽的星球。
example.pinyin: Dìqiú shì yí gè měilì de xīngqiú.
example.english: Earth is a beautiful celestial body.
example.fact: 星球 combines 星 ("star," any bright point in the sky) with 球 ("ball, sphere") to describe any round heavenly body in general — planets, moons, and stars alike — while 行星 is reserved specifically for "planet," a distinction easy to blur when translating casually from English.

examples.hanzi: 夜里,天空中有很多星球。
examples.pinyin: Yèlǐ, tiānkōng zhōng yǒu hěn duō xīngqiú.
examples.english: At night, there are many stars and planets in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 他想知道其他星球上有没有生命。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zhīdào qítā xīngqiú shang yǒu méiyǒu shēngmìng.
examples.english: He wants to know if there is life on other planets.

components.note: 录 (lù) gives sound to 绿 lǜ, 禄 lù and 碌 lù; as a word it means to record.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 像 is a person's likeness.
象 (xiàng, elephant) gives the exact sound; 象 first meant elephant, then "image".

example.pinyin: Wǒmen gěi hūnlǐ lùxiàng le.
example.english: We recorded a video of the wedding.
example.fact: 录像 literally means "to record (录) an image (像)" — coined for videotape technology, it has stuck around in everyday Mandarin even in the smartphone era, sitting alongside the newer, more casual 拍视频 ("to shoot a video") as an older but still standard way to talk about recording video.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用手机录像。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng shǒujī lùxiàng.
examples.english: You can record a video with your phone.

examples.hanzi: 警察查看了路口的录像。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá chákàn le lùkǒu de lùxiàng.
examples.english: The police checked the footage from the intersection.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.
广 (building) — 广 is a building or wide roof, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 store; 序 is order and sequence.
予 (yǔ) — near sound — 序 is xù; 予 also sounds out 预 yù and 野 yě.

example.hanzi: 这是一个新的电脑程序。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè xīn de diànnǎo chéngxù.
example.english: This is a new computer program.
example.fact: 程序 meant "sequence, order, procedure" long before computers existed — a bureaucratic and legal term for following the correct steps, as in 法律程序 ("legal procedure") — and simply extended naturally to name a piece of software once Chinese needed a word for "the ordered sequence of instructions a computer follows."

examples.hanzi: 办理这个手续要走三道程序。
examples.pinyin: Bànlǐ zhège shǒuxù yào zǒu sān dào chéngxù.
examples.english: This procedure takes three steps.

examples.hanzi: 我正在学写电脑程序。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài xué xiě diànnǎo chéngxù.
examples.english: I'm learning to write computer programs.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.

example.pinyin: Zhè fèn qíngbào fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.english: This piece of intelligence is extremely important.
example.fact: 情报 leans toward the "intelligence" sense of English "information" — secret, strategic, or military data gathered on purpose — which is why it's the standard word in spy fiction and espionage news (情报机构, "intelligence agency") rather than a synonym for the neutral 信息 or 消息.

examples.hanzi: 他们从网上得到了重要的情报。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen cóng wǎng shang dédào le zhòngyào de qíngbào.
examples.english: They got important information from the internet.

examples.hanzi: 这个情报是谁告诉你的?
examples.pinyin: Zhège qíngbào shì shéi gàosu nǐ de?
examples.english: Who told you this intelligence?

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 刺 is to stab.
朿 (cì) — 朿 is a thorn and gives the sound — 刺 is cì, same syllable.

example.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, méigui yǒu cì.
example.english: Be careful, the rose has thorns.
example.fact: 刺 is both the thorn and the act of stabbing: 刺伤, 刺绣 (embroidery), 刺猬 (hedgehog). 刺激 is stimulation and can be a thrill: 很刺激 means "exciting".

examples.hanzi: 他的手被刺扎了一下。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒu bèi cì zhā le yíxià.
examples.english: His hand was pricked by a thorn.

examples.hanzi: 他刺了一刀，被警察抓走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā cì le yì dāo, bèi jǐngchá zhuā zǒu le.
examples.english: He stabbed someone once and was taken away by the police.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks fire and heat, as in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp, 烟 smoke; 炒 is stir-frying over fire.
少 (shǎo) — close sound: 炒 chǎo. 少 also sounds out 吵 chǎo and 抄 chāo.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī chǎofàn.
example.english: I want to eat fried rice.
example.fact: 炒 is the high-heat wok technique central to Chinese cooking: 炒饭, 炒面, 炒菜. It also means to speculate (炒股, to play the stock market), to hype (炒作), and 炒鱿鱼 (fire someone) because squid curls up like a bedroll when stir-fried.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈在厨房炒菜。
examples.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng chǎocài.
examples.english: Mom is stir-frying dishes in the kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 他想炒几个青菜来下饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chǎo jǐ gè qīngcài lái xiàfàn.
examples.english: He wants to stir-fry some greens to go with rice.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 — 绪 first meant the end of a thread, then the clue, as in 头绪, and mood, as in 情绪.
者 (zhě) — loose hint — 绪 is xù.

example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān qíngxù bú tài hǎo.
example.english: He's not in a great mood today.
example.fact: 情绪 technically covers the whole range of emotional states, but in casual speech it's overwhelmingly used to flag something negative (闹情绪, "to sulk"; 情绪化, "moody, emotionally volatile") — similar to how English "emotional" often implies "upset" even though it just means "having emotions."

examples.hanzi: 听音乐可以让我的情绪变好。
examples.pinyin: Tīng yīnyuè kěyǐ ràng wǒ de qíngxù biàn hǎo.
examples.english: Listening to music can improve my mood.

examples.hanzi: 她的情绪很容易受天气影响。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qíngxù hěn róngyì shòu tiānqì yǐngxiǎng.
examples.english: Her mood is easily affected by the weather.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: a strange feeling.
圣 here is not the "sage" word; it is only a loose sound clue for guài.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 孩子害怕床底下有怪物。
example.pinyin: Háizi hàipà chuáng dǐxia yǒu guàiwu.
example.english: The child is afraid there's a monster under the bed.
example.fact: 怪 alone already means "strange, odd," and 物 means "thing, creature" — 怪物 builds "monster" the plain way, as "a strange creature," and can extend loosely to an eccentric or unconventional person, much like English can call an odd genius "a bit of a monster" affectionately.

examples.hanzi: 这个电影里有一个很可怕的怪物。
examples.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng lǐ yǒu yí ge hěn kěpà de guàiwu.
examples.english: There is a very scary monster in this movie.

examples.hanzi: 大家都说他是个怪物,因为他从不睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu shuō tā shì ge guàiwu, yīnwèi tā cóng bú shuìjiào.
examples.english: Everyone says he's a freak because he never sleeps.
